verdicts.summary: The CSRF token is bound to the DPoP session id, and the client can renew its token between the approval and decision calls. The decision then fails with a misleading message, and Approve stays broken until a page reload.
verdicts.scenario: 1) The owner opens /approve-agent with a cached T3 Connect token that is 59 minutes old (DPoP ttl is 1h, exchangeBootstrapCredentialForAccessToken:986). Approval succeeds and the details carry csrfToken = sign(sessionId_A, ...). 2) The owner takes more than a few seconds to choose a level. 3) On Approve, getDpopToken rejects the cached token because expiry is within DPOP_ACCESS_TOKEN_REFRESH_SKEW_MS (60s, model.ts:137) and exchanges token B. Relay grants do not replace the earlier session (replaceActiveForSubjectAndMethod only applies to desktop-bootstrap, EnvironmentAuth.ts:989), so B has a new session id. 4) The decision carries the old csrfToken. approve() compares it with csrf(sessionId_B) and fails with 'Your session cannot approve this request. Enter a pairing code instead.' (McpOAuth.ts:477-479). 5) That message is shown as a refusal. This page has no code field, and McpConsent does not reload details after a decision error (ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:211-220), so every retry sends the same stale csrf and fails the same way until the owner reloads. The decision call has no isUnauthorizedResponse check (connectMcpApproval.ts:99-106). The chance of hitting this is about consent-time / token-lifetime, so a few percent of sign-ins.
verdicts.consequence: The owner sees a dead-end error that tells them to enter a code the page cannot take. Approving works again only after a reload. The note calls this 'rare' but does not handle it.
verdicts.missing: Re-run the approval call (get a fresh csrfToken) when the decision answer is the session/CSRF refusal, or pin the token between load and decide.

verdicts.summary: The authorize call sits outside the 10s bound, but the token exchange has its own 30s cap and every timeout becomes a retryable error. I found no hang.
verdicts.scenario: The relay hangs during the first token exchange at connectMcpApproval.ts:64. I also tried a revoked token, where the approval retry would force a second exchange inside the 10s loop timeout.

verdicts.summary: Adding `headers: OptionalBearerHeaders` leaves no caller without headers, and DPoP-style authorization values pass the schema.
verdicts.scenario: I looked for a caller that omits headers and for a DPoP authorization value that the schema would reject. All callers pass headers (ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:110,113; PeerLinks.ts:312; connectMcpApproval.ts:93,104). The schema accepts any string for `authorization` and `dpop`, so `DPoP <token>` passes. Cross-origin calls from app.t3.codes are allowed because production CORS uses the default wildcard origin without credentials.

verdicts.summary: The only hazard I could build is the one in finding 0: a visitor to the tunnel who is not the T3 Connect owner is redirected automatically and has no code fallback.

The flag is always true, but its only reader is the wizard, and the wizard only reaches the Connect step once the managed tunnel gate is open. The hosted-redirect condition on the server is checked against the same tunnel host.
verdicts.scenario: The flag reads true while the environment is not linked or not on a managed tunnel, so the wizard would drop the code step for an environment the server will not redirect to the hosted app. The wizard cannot open in that case.

verdicts.summary: The client redirect check accepts every redirect URI the server can register, including IPv6 loopback.
verdicts.scenario: A registered `http://[::1]:PORT/cb` redirect. URL.hostname returns '[::1]', and isLoopbackHost accepts it explicitly. 127.0.0.1 and localhost also pass, and `HTTP://LOCALHOST` is normalised by URL. The server accepts only https or those three loopback hosts.

verdicts.summary: Load answers and redirects are guarded against stale or unsafe results. The one stale-details problem I found belongs to note 0, not this note.
verdicts.scenario: A load answer that arrives after unmount or after the authorization changes, and a load that returns a redirect to a non-http(s) address. I found no other way to reach a stale-state bug.

verdicts.summary: The redirect gate refuses javascript: and data:. The address the server returns always comes from a registered redirect URI.
verdicts.scenario: The environment returns a `javascript:` or `http://evil` URL after approval or denial. agentRedirectUrl returns null, so window.location.replace is not called and an error is shown.

verdicts.summary: The open question about the managed remote-clients policy is finding 4. Its fallback-link dead end is findings 3 and 0. I checked the server: it has no `remoteClients` check, and the managed runtime-mode ceiling is enforced when the agent calls tools (McpHttpServer.ts:201-235), not at approval. So the wizard's denial display was the only gate on that path.
Failures are squashed to the typed error or a defect, and the page maps both to a message. Each run builds its own atom, so concurrent calls do not share state.
verdicts.scenario: A typed failure or a defect from the command, and two overlapping load/decide runs.

verdicts.summary: Environments on the previous release still send users from their own /connect-agent page to the hosted /approve-agent page with the old handoff parameters. The rewritten hosted page ignores those parameters, so the 'Approve with T3 Connect' button on those environments ends on an error page.
verdicts.scenario: 1) A user's environment runs the previous release. Its /connect-agent page showed a button built by approveAgentUrl (the deleted apps/web/src/cloud/connectAgentApproval.ts:451-461 in the diff), which opens https://app.t3.codes/approve-agent?environment=..&access=..&nonce=..&return_to=<sign-in page URL>. 2) The hosted app is deployed with this commit. The new /approve-agent reads only `environment` plus the OAuth parameters (readAuthorizationRequest, ConnectAgentSurface.tsx:120-122), and the old link carries none of the OAuth parameters. 3) The page calls approval with an empty payload through the relay. validateAuthorization fails with 'unknown app' (McpOAuth.ts:363-368), or on an older server the call returns no csrfToken. 4) The user sees 'This sign-in cannot continue'. The original OAuth query exists only inside `return_to`, which the page does not read, so the user must restart the sign-in from the agent.
verdicts.consequence: The agent sign-in button on every not-yet-upgraded T3 Connect environment stops working as soon as the hosted app deploys, because hosted-app deployment is decoupled from environment updates.
verdicts.missing: Keep reading the old `access`/`nonce`/`return_to` parameters on /approve-agent (or redirect them back to `return_to`), or hold the hosted deploy until older environments have updated.
